message.content:
The sea usually appears **blue**—the same hue you see when looking at clear sky‑water mixtures. That’s because sunlight hits the ocean surface; shorter wavelengths (blues) scatter more than longer ones (reds), so we perceive a predominantly blue tone.  

However, the exact shade changes depending on several factors:

| Factor | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Depth & clarity | Deeper, clearer waters look darker navy/indigo; shallow sandy bottoms reflect light back as turquoise or greenish hues. |
| Algae / phytoplankton | High concentrations give a greener tint. |
| Sediment & runoff | Muddy or polluted areas may appear brownish or murky. |
| Sun angle & time of day | Early morning or late afternoon rays make the sea glow orange/red; midday sun gives a bright azure. |

So while “blue” is the classic description, real seas display a spectrum from deep indigo to pale teal, sometimes even green or brown under certain conditions.
